status: PROPOSED, NOT AUTHORISED, NOT RUN. Before any game: operator approval, then freeze (journal 'v5-preregistered' with this file's sha256, policiesHash, the reference hashes and evidence/balance/v5/policy-checks.json sha256).
question: Do the balance patterns observed so far (first/second-mover advantage, Human/AI-side asymmetry, game length, opening collapse) survive a change of the policy that generates the observations?
scope: Self-play with three engine-based policies. Conclusions about a policy describe that policy. A pattern is called a RULE-LEVEL CANDIDATE only if it survives all three; even then it says nothing about human players.

policies.definition: server/balance/v5/policies.ts planOpponentAware: own symmetric candidate set, exact own move-phase ends (rank strata 8), worst case over every opponent placement option + its greedy moves, maximin; top 6 candidates; deterministic
server/balance/v5/policies.ts planSoftmax: reference scores, k = 4, T = 1.3255 (half the reference reply model's measured mean prediction error 2.651), floor 0.02, sampled from public seed + turn

mandatoryRequirements.hiddenRngInvariance: decision unchanged when only the hidden RNG differs: 0 changes allowed (evidence/balance/v5/policy-checks.json, 40 positions + tests)
mandatoryRequirements.mirrorSymmetry: position and its mirror give the mirrored decision and score: 0 mismatches allowed for oa-v1 and softmax-v1; for the frozen reference the residual is reported and accepted only by explicit operator decision
mandatoryRequirements.executor: all policies use the reference EV executor with K1 for moves (re-plan after teleports)

seeds.note: fresh. Not used before: V4 pilot 64001-64030, V4.2 dev 66001-66030, holdout 65001-65060 (untouched), decision probes 67901-67930 (no game), smoke 99001-99499

arms.design: 10 seeds x each policy on each side x each first mover

estimatedCost: about 30-45 min wall time with 6 workers on this PC (oa-v1 about 3.4 s per decision); 0 Kane, 0 external calls

metrics.moverBalance: first-mover decisive win rate; Wilson 95% and opening-cluster bootstrap 95% (games grouped by their first two turns, side-relative)
metrics.roleSymmetry: Human-side decisive win rate; same two intervals
metrics.strategicDiversity: distinct two-turn openings, opening entropy (bits), effective openings 2^H, largest opening share, distinct placement signatures, normalized effect entropy
metrics.strength: Bradley-Terry log-strength vs the reference from cross-play (bootstrap 95%), pairwise decisive win rates (Wilson)
metrics.length: mean, median, 90th percentile turns, turn-limit rate, draws
metrics.counterplay: lead changes per game, comeback rate
metrics.openingPatterns: frequency table of side-relative openings per policy; turn-2 captures per game
metrics.integrity: illegal moves, errors, softlocks, engine replay of every game, teleport foresight (V3 method) must contain 0

decisionRules.policyLevel: For each policy separately: first-mover and Human-side edges (rate - 0.5) with opening-cluster intervals; length and diversity reported. These are statements about that policy.
decisionRules.validityForRuleClaims: A policy counts toward a rule-level claim only if its self-play has at least 3 effective openings (2^H >= 3). Fewer means its games observe too few distinct situations to speak for the rules.
decisionRules.survival: For a pattern measured as (rate - 0.5): SURVIVES (rule-level candidate) if every valid policy's opening-cluster interval lies beyond +0.05 (or every one beyond -0.05); POLICY-SPECIFIC if one valid policy shows it beyond 0.05 and another's interval lies within +-0.05 or beyond 0.05 the other way; INCONCLUSIVE otherwise, or if fewer than 2 policies are valid.
decisionRules.length: a long-game pattern SURVIVES if every valid policy has turn-limit rate >= 15% (Wilson lower bound >= 0.10); POLICY-SPECIFIC if one is >= 15% and another's upper bound < 10%
decisionRules.strength: reported, not a gate. A policy that loses heavily to the reference is still informative about the rules; its weakness is stated next to its balance numbers.
decisionRules.noPromotion: Nothing from this protocol is promoted; the holdout stays reserved for a later, separately approved, frozen candidate.
